cases.idea: Washington Dulles International Airport's expanded main terminal and original Saarinen control tower
cases.composition: Expanded 1996 terminal, not the original 600-foot building. Include the original tower only with reference-supported placement. No runways, midfield concourses or parking lots. Declare the chosen front view.
criticalChecks: No airfield invented around the terminal
Terminal and tower heights are distinct
Front/back arrangement follows the actual references
The expanded terminal is not assigned the original terminal's length
unverified: Exact roof cross-section and tower offset need a viewable reference before numeric assertions

cases.idea: Golden Gate Bridge suspension span, two towers and cables
cases.composition: Only the 6,450-foot suspension portion: 4,200-foot main span and equal 1,125-foot side spans. Exclude approach roads and scenery from bridge measurements. Keep actual proportions; disclose any stud-scale rounding.
criticalChecks: Main span about 3.73 times either side span
Tower height above road is not confused with height above water
unverified: Physical cable tension cannot be certified by this catalog's stud-contact audit

cases.composition: Apollo configuration with three propulsion stages, spacecraft and escape tower. Rocket only; no launch tower or platform. Preserve slender proportions.
criticalChecks: Apollo configuration rather than two-stage Skylab
No launch infrastructure counted in rocket bounds
111-metre overall height is not assigned to a single stage
unverified: Stage-length ratios and diameter require an additional dimensioned reference

cases.idea: Washington Dulles International Airport as a complete airport site
cases.composition: Use a dated airfield plan. Include the main terminal, concourses and runways in their actual arrangement. Do not replace the whole airport with a terminal-only model or invent symmetry.
criticalChecks: No invented runway orientations or duplicated layout
unverified: Requires a current airfield plan; a passenger terminal map alone is insufficient
